content.text: Prolonged exposure to anthropogenic noise (sounds from human sources like traffic or mining) can affect animals, as Hansjoerg P. Kunc and colleagues showed in a 2014 study of mollusks. This effect is so common that biologists Hansjoerg P. Kunc and Rouven Schmidt consider anthropogenic noise a serious form of pollution. In a meta-analysis of more than 100 studies of anthropogenic noise and various species and classes of animals, Kunc and Schmidt found that, on average, mammals showed larger effects from the noise than mollusks did. Therefore, their results suggest that conservationists focused on the well-being of mammals will likely find that <u>          </u>

prompt.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

content.text: issues related to anthropogenic noise are more important to their work than they would be to the work of conservationists focused on mollusks.
addressing issues related to anthropogenic noise for mammals could worsen the effects of anthropogenic noise on mollusks.
issues related to anthropogenic noise are easier to address in their work than they would be in the work of conservationists focused on mollusks.
anthropogenic noise is responsible for some of the issues that have previously been attributed to other causes.

Exclusively inhabiting tropical countries such as Liberia, wild chimpanzees lack adaptations to seasonal variations in ultraviolet B (UVB) irradiance from sunlight; since UVB exposure enables vertebrates to synthesize vitamin D, this raises questions about how chimpanzees in mid-latitude zoos are affected by the seasonal variations in UVB irradiance that occur in those locations. In a study of zoo chimpanzees in Norway and other mid-latitude countries, Sophie Moittié and colleagues found that vitamin D levels are lower in autumn than in summer, paralleling UVB irradiance, but also that regardless of season, chimpanzees with unlimited outdoor access have higher vitamin D levels than chimpanzees with limited outdoor access. These findings suggest that <u>          </u>

prompt.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

content.text: the amount of outdoor access received by zoo chimpanzees in Norway and other mid-latitude countries affects those chimpanzees’ vitamin D levels more than do seasonal variations in UVB irradiance.
adaptations to seasonal variations in UVB irradiance may be emerging in zoo chimpanzees with unlimited outdoor access in Norway and other mid-latitude countries.
in mid-latitude countries such as Norway, zoo chimpanzees with unlimited outdoor access tend to synthesize more vitamin D per unit of UVB irradiance in summer than they do in autumn.
giving zoo chimpanzees in Norway and other mid-latitude countries unlimited outdoor access during autumn may help offset the effect of reduced UVB irradiance relative to summer.

Neurobiologists Laura Cuaya, Raúl Hernández-Pérez, and colleagues investigated the language detection abilities of eighteen dogs raised in similar settings. The researchers monitored the brain activity of Bran (a border collie), Alma (a mixed breed), and other dogs while the animals listened to three recordings: one of The Little Prince being read in Spanish the second in Hungarian, and a third made up of short, randomly selected fragments of the first two, scrambled so that they didn't resemble human speech. Each dog was familiar with either Spanish or Hungarian, but not both. The team concluded that the amount of previous language exposure a dog has received may influence its ability to distinguish familiar languages from unfamiliar ones.

prompt.text: Which finding from the study, if true, would most directly support the team's conclusion?

content.text: The similarity between the pattern of brain activity a dog showed in response to hearing the scrambled recording and the pattern of brain activity it showed in response to hearing the language it was not accustomed to was greatest among older dogs.

Dogs showed a different pattern of brain activity when hearing the language they were accustomed to than when hearing the scrambled recording, and the difference in brain activity increased with the age of the dog scanned.

The difference between the pattern of brain activity a dog showed when hearing the language it was accustomed to and the pattern of brain activity it showed when hearing the language it was not accustomed to was greatest among older dogs.

Although the dogs’ general hearing sensitivity declined with age, dogs of all ages showed more brain activity in response to hearing the language they were accustomed to than in response to hearing the other language.

By combining dense synthesizer arrangements and metallic percussion with a recorded voice electronically shifted in pitch above its natural range, Scottish musician Sophie exemplified the style of contemporary electronic music known as hyperpop. This style is elastic enough to include Shygirl, who incorporates R&B vocal stylings into the hyperpop sound, as well. The style’s inclusivity has been encouraged—excessively so, many fans say—by the music-streaming service Spotify, whose popular playlist of hyperpop songs balances core figures with distinct outliers, like 1980s icon Kate Bush.

prompt.text: Based on the text, what is one effect of the Spotify playlist?

content.text: It has promoted the typical hyperpop style at the expense of hyperpop songs diverging from that style.
It has annoyed some hyperpop listeners by including music that isn’t typical of the style.
It has alienated the hyperpop audience by excluding artists who helped found the style.
It has exerted undue influence on established hyperpop artists to modify their style.

The bird species *Momotus momota* (the Amazonian motmot) practices a foraging strategy known as sallying (catching insects in flight and returning to a perch to eat them), enabling it to scan for prey and predators simultaneously. *Glyphorynchus spirurus* (the wedge-billed woodcreeper), on the other hand, practices bark gleaning (picking insects off the bark of trees), substantially limiting the bird’s field of vision while foraging. Biologist Ari Martínez and colleagues, who studied the ecological community these species share in French Guiana, hypothesized that avian foraging strategies that reduce individual vigilance are associated with greater reliance on other species to watch for predators.

prompt.text: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Martínez and colleagues’ hypothesis?

content.text: Martínez and colleagues observed that G. spirurus regularly joined multispecies flocks, whereas M. momota rarely or never did.
Martínez and colleagues found that the predator alarm calls of M. momota and G. spirurus have a high degree of acoustic similarity.
When Martínez and colleagues played alarm calls from another local bird species, M. momota displayed predator-avoidance behavior, whereas G. spirurus did not display any behavioral change.
Of several species practicing bark gleaning that Martínez and colleagues observed, only G. spirurus routinely associated with other species.

The phrase usa-don sonda is a future-oriented expression used by members of the Yupno, an Indigenous group in Papua New Guinea, that translates to “next week.” Rafael Núñez and colleagues recorded Yupno speakers explaining several of these temporal-related words and phrases and coded each speaker’s manual gestures. Previous research has found evidence of English speakers referring to the left/right axis to describe events in time, and many researchers believe that this tendency to make temporal distinctions along imagined linear axes is universal. However, Núñez and colleagues claim that this tendency is not in fact ubiquitous.

prompt.text: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Núñez and colleagues’ claim?

content.text: When outdoors and referring to the future, Yupno speakers facing uphill gesture in front of themselves, whereas those facing downhill gesture behind themselves.
Yupno speakers were observed making temporal gestures both indoors and outdoors, though with greater frequency when indoors.
Some Yupno grammatical structures used when talking about time are also used in English.
Yupno speakers typically use their left hand to make temporal gestures regardless of whether the gestures are past oriented or future oriented.

When read sequentially, the individual sonnets of a sonnet cycle—a series of fourteen-line poems that rhyme in a fixed pattern—typically evince a loose narrative arc that traditionally dramatizes the speaker’s persistent efforts to win the affections of an aloof addressee, as occurs in Edmund Spenser’s 1595 *Amoretti*. However, by using the sonnet cycle to instead relay a loosely autobiographical account of his travels abroad, modern poet Claude McKay’s series “Cities” subverts entrenched sonnet conventions to reveal the form’s potential for new possibilities.

prompt.text: Which statement about sonnet cycles is best supported by the text?

content.text: Although sonnet cycles generally present an overarching narrative structure, some of those narratives, such as the narrative in McKay’s “Cities,” are more cohesive than others.
Although the rigidity of the conventions of sonnet cycles discourages experimentation, sonnet cycles sometimes exhibit truly novel features, as exemplified by McKay’s “Cities” and Spenser’s Amoretti.

Although sonnet cycles generally feature similar narrative arcs related to the speaker’s relationship with another person, there is a remarkable range in the number of perspectives represented within the story arcs of different sonnet cycles.
Although sonnet cycles are strongly associated with a certain subject matter, this association doesn’t preclude poets from exploring ideas that are relatively unorthodox by the genre’s standards.

The Bronze Age in Britain lasted from around 2500 BCE to approximately 700 BCE. Collections of metal items (called hoards) from all periods of the Bronze Age have been found in Britain, including the Arreton Down hoard of artifacts from the 17th century BCE, unearthed around 1735, and the much later Hollingbourne hoard of artifacts from the 10th century BCE, unearthed around 2003. Sometime in the Middle Bronze Age (approximately from the 14th century BCE to the 10th century BCE), metalsmiths in Britain began to develop swords for the first time. This fact helps explain why, whereas evidence of sword production was found in\_\_\_

prompt.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

content.text: both the Arreton Down hoard and the Hollingbourne hoard, only the latter included evidence of more refined sword production.
hoards discovered before 2003, no such evidence was found in hoards that were discovered later.
the Arreton Down hoard, no intact swords were found among the items in the hoard.
the Hollingbourne hoard, no such evidence was found in the Arreton Down hoard.

Mongolia, which, according to international indices, has relatively strong democratic institutions and low intranational income inequality, experienced an inflation rate of 4.30% in 2017, whereas Cameroon, which shows the opposite pattern on such indices, had an inflation rate of only 0.64% that year. Such comparisons have engendered speculation that by diluting control over the economy, democratic institutions inhibit states' ability to counteract inflationary pressures. To test this possibility systematically, Raj Desai et al. examined democratic strength, intranational inequality, and inflation in more than 100 countries, finding that democratic strength, if associated with low inequality, restrains inflationary pressures, suggesting that \_\_\_\_\_\_

prompt.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

content.text: it would be a mistake to treat the relative inflation rates of Mongolia and Cameroon as indicative of an inherent shortcoming in democratic institutions with regard to control over inflation.

speculations about the relative inability of democratic institutions to counteract inflation are based on measures that tend to exaggerate the levels of inflation in strongly democratic countries such as Mongolia.

the factors that contributed to Mongolia's elevated inflation rate relative to Cameroon's have less to do with the countries' political institutions than with the countries' levels of income inequality.
the difference between Mongolia and Cameroon with regard to democratic institution strength may have been greater in 2017 than was represented by international indices.

Scholars are increasingly exploring the communication and preservation of ecological knowledge through Indigenous songs (e. g Sakha songs about local ecosystems and those of the Kaluli people about rainforest sounds). In one study, ethnobiologist Dana Lepofsky et al. received insight from Kwaxsistalla Wathl‘thla, a song keeper for the Kwakwaka‘wakw people in Canada, into songs referencing the people's use of terraced gardens in intertidal zones along the Pacific Northwest coast for the cultivation of clams for consumption. Archaeological evidence of significant increases in clam size and abundance in that area concurrent with the documented past implementation of the method described in the songs supports the conclusion that \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

prompt.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

content.text: although contemporary Kwakwaka'wakw people have a deep understanding of and appreciation for the fishing and farming practices used by their ancestors, they no longer implement those methods.
there is greater corroboration in the archaeological record of ecological practices described in Kwakwaka‘wakw songs than of those described in Sakha and Kaluli songs.
the practice used by ancestors of modern Kwakwaka'wakw people not only effectively maintained a food source but also promoted its robustness.
non-Indigenous people around the Pacific Northwest coast adopted the practice developed by the Kwakwaka'wakw people after observing its efficacy.

Arthurian legends (tales related to the character of King Arthur) derive from many sources, such as *Englynion y Beddau*, composed between the 9th and 10th centuries, and *Sir Gawain and the Green Knight* from the 1300s. One of the most significant sources, Geoffrey of Monmouth's *History of the Kings of Britain*, was written in Latin in the 1130s; some material from it was later adapted by the Norman poet Wace into the *Roman de Brut* in 1155. But while no source before 1155 includes references to the famous Round Table at which Arthur's knights assembled, both the *Roman de Brut* and Sir Thomas Malory's 15th-century compilation of Arthurian legends, *Le Morte d'Arthur*, do. It can therefore be inferred that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Geoffrey of Monmouth's accounts of Arthurian legends in his  *History* are more similar overall in content to the accounts in *Sir Gawain and the Green  Knight* than they are to the accounts in  *Roman de Brut*.

An analysis by Alain Elayi and colleagues of coins minted in Sidon in the fifth and fourth centuries BCE reveals a change in their composition overtime: while a coin from circa 450 BCE contains about 98% silver and 1% copper, a coin from 367 BCE (the end of Ba’alsillem II’s reign) contains 74.2% silver and 24.7% copper, giving it a relatively yellowish appearance that traders would have noticed. Because coins with a silver content below 80% were widely considered unsuitable for trade, Elayi et al. speculate that a crisis in confidence in the currency occurred in Sidon around 367 BCE, which was likely relieved—despite Sidon’s persistent oppressive financial obligations—as a result of Ba’alsillem II’s successor Abd’astart I’s decision to \_\_\_\_\_\_

prompt.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

content.text: keep the amount of silver in Sidonian coins consistent with that in coins minted in 367 BCE but decrease their weight.
proclaim that the percentage of silver in coins suitable for trade would be raised to a threshold higher than 80%.
fund the mining of some copper deposits that were not available to Ba'alsillem Il.
begin minting heavier coins with a proportion of silver to copper similar to that in coins minted in 367 BCE.

Exclusively inhabiting tropical countries such as Tanzania, wild chimpanzees lack adaptations to seasonal variations in ultraviolet B (UVB) irradiance from sunlight; since UVB exposure enables vertebrates to synthesize vitamin D, this raises questions about how chimpanzees in mid-laltitude zoos are affected by the lower and more variable UVB irradiance in those locations. In a study of zoo chimpanzees in France and other mid-latitude countries, Sophie Moittié and colleagues found not only that chimpanzees' vitamin D levels correlate with UVB irradiance but also that vitamin D levels show no evidence of plateauing as UVB irradiance reaches its highest local levels, suggesting that \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

content.text: adaptations to seasonal variations in UVB irradiance may be emerging in ZOO chimpanzees in France and other mid-latitude countries.
averaged across seasons, vitamin D levels in zoo chimpanzees in mid-latitude countries such as France tend to be comparable to those in wild chimpanzees in tropical countries such as Tanzania.

Optimal foraging theory (OFT) holds that animals' foraging behaviors reflect cost-benefit trade offs that vary by species and with dynamic ecological circumstances. One such circumstance is lunar intensity, which Alexander Lang and colleagues found to be negatively associated with foraging by white—throated round eared bats but Patricia C. Wright found to be positively associated with foraging by three-striped night monkeys. This discrepancy is explicable in terms of OFT: the monkeys' greater reliance on vision means that higher lunar intensity benefits them more than it benefits the bats.

prompt.text: According to the text, the difference between Lang and colleagues' findings and Wright's findings can be attributed to which difference between white throated round-eared bats and three striped night monkeys?

content.text: The bats are less reliant on vision than the monkeys are.
The bats decrease their foraging activity as lunar intensity increases, whereas the monkeys increase their foraging activity.
The bats are more vulnerable to predators than the monkeys are.
The bats encounter different levels of lunar intensity than the monkeys do.

Water flowing around an obstruction creates vortices (swirls) that vary in size with the obstruction's size and position, and fish sense these vortices in order to navigate around the obstructions. Using models of three fish-head shapes—narrow (low ratio of width to length), intermediate, and wide (high ratio of width to length)—Yuzo R. Yanagisuru, Otar Akanyetl, and James C. Liao showed that as vortex size increases, pressure fluctuations at the snout increase for narrow-headed and intermediate-headed fish but remain low for wide-headed fish. A second research team has therefore hypothesized that in low visibility, a fish will be more likely to avoid an obstruction when the associated pressure fluctuations at the fish's snout are greater.

prompt.text: Which finding, if true, would most directly challenge the second research team's hypothesis?

content.text: A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the Synodontis macropunctata, which has a relatively wide head, bumped into less than half of the obstructions

A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the intermediate-headed dusky smooth-hound (Musreluscanis) bumped into the obstructions just as often as the wide-headed Synodontis macropunctata did.

A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the wide-headed Synodontis macropunctata bumped into obstructions more often than the intermediate-headed dusky smooth-hound(Mustelus canis) did.

A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that some specimens of the intermediate-headed dusky smooth-hound (Mustelus canis) bumped into the obstructions more often than others did.
